text:
alex: Heads-up — legal sent back the cloud term sheet from CloudCorp. They're asking for a 24-month commit with a regional floor and preemption windows. I'm pulling together ops concerns before we hand this to finance. Thoughts?

maya: Can you paste the exact regional floor wording? need to see if it's per-region or global.

alex: Pasted snippet from the draft: `Customer agrees to a minimum committed spend of $4.2M over 24 months, with a per-region 60% availability floor subject to provider confirmation.`

dan: 60% availability floor is weird — we want guaranteed capacity not availability percent. are they counting on preemption to reach that?

sam: also flag metering: our usage mixes p4/p5/xcpu credits. we need clear SKUs + ability to map credits across GPU families during migration. otherwise we get charged at wrong rates.

liya: ops asks: 1) explicit non-preemptible pool for reserved capacity (or SLA-backed replacement), 2) right to burst across regions for 48 hrs without extra penalty, 3) ability to convert unused commit into near-term credits (90d) if they fail availability.

billing-bot: FYI — historical usage for last 12 months: p5h: 1.8M hours, p4d: 620k hours, multi-region split: us-west 55%, eu-west 30%, ap-south 15% (link: https://billing.internal/redwood/usage).

maya: we should propose an alternative clause: `Provider shall guarantee reserved instances with <1% preemption for dedicated pools; in outage events Provider will (a) provide immediate capacity reallocation within same region or (b) apply credits equal to unserved hours at 2x rate.`

dan: +1. Also negotiate an explicit burst allowance: `Customer may burst up to 30% over committed capacity in other regions for cumulative 48 hours per month.`

alex: Good. On credits: finance wants a convert-to-commit option (apply credits to future committed spend) vs cash refunds. Ops prefers credits with loosened SKU mapping so we can spend across GPU families.

sam: One more ops detail — network egress caps per region. If they throttle egress on dedicated instances, our latency SLOs fail. Need a clause that network egress for dedicated pools is metered and cannot be throttled below X Gbps per instance type.

liya: I'll draft an ops appendix with these three bullets and examples. Example failure remediation flow (short):
```
1) Provider detects <99.5% capacity match for reserved pool -> 6-hr notice to customer
2) Provider offers immediate region-level replacement or credits at 3x unserved token-hours
3) If no replacement within 12 hrs, customer may re-route to fallback models without charge
```

alex: Perfect — try to keep language tight; legal will rewrite. Also call out SLA measurement: use provider's internal capacity logs but allow Redwood to audit once per quarter.

maya: who owns the negotiation call? ops should join with finance. I can present the appendix.

alex: Great — set up time. Can we target EOD Tue to get draft to finance?

dan: I'll run a quick risk calc on impact if they enforce region floors and preemption. give me 24 hrs.

liya: draft will include toggles we can hand to sales (e.g., 36mo vs 24mo, ROI numbers, and fallback credit multipliers).

alex: Thanks team — please keep comments inline on the appendix doc. tagging @maya @dan @liya for next steps. :thumbsup:
